slot: GST: threshold, export of services, LUT, OIDAR, reverse charge (VERIFY WITH A CA)

pick.name: Stay unregistered below Rs20 lakh aggregate turnover; register (Rule 14A fast-track) + file LUT before first zero-rated export once over it
pick.what: Exports of services are zero-rated; LUT (RFD-11, per FY) lets you export without paying IGST
pick.why: Notification 10/2017-Integrated Tax exempts inter-state service suppliers up to Rs20 lakh (Rs10 lakh special-category states) from registration; exports count in aggregate turnover
pick.free_limits: Threshold Rs20 lakh services (unchanged); aggregate turnover INCLUDES exports; LUT needs a GSTIN; Rule 14A (from 2025-11-01) grants registration in 3 working days if B2B output tax <= Rs2.5 lakh/month

alts.name: Voluntary registration from day one
alts.what: Register early, file LUT, claim ITC
alts.why: Needed to sell to GST-registered Indian businesses with ITC, or to recover 18% paid on foreign tools via RCM + refunds

candidates.name: Voluntary registration
candidates.verdict: Alt: when B2B India clients want GST invoices or you want ITC

candidates.name: Export with IGST paid + refund (no LUT)
candidates.verdict: Rejected: blocks cash until refund; LUT is free

decision: Below Rs20 lakh (including export receipts) you need not register for pure services under Notification 10/2017-IT, but the moment you need LUT/ITC or Indian B2B invoicing, register via Rule 14A. Foreign SaaS you buy: while unregistered, foreign OIDAR vendors must charge you 18% IGST themselves (since 2023-10-01 any unregistered recipient is a 'non-taxable online recipient'); once registered, give them your GSTIN and pay IGST under reverse charge, then claim ITC.
details: VERIFY WITH A CA: (1) whether Notification 10/2017-IT covers export-only suppliers; (2) MoR payouts: supply to a foreign MoR entity is likely export of service, but Dodo's INR-wallet payouts for Indian buyers may be a domestic supply to an Indian entity; (3) compulsory registration for RCM payers (s24) vs the OIDAR rule; (4) export invoice wording under LUT.

verify.note: Confirmed from CBIC official text: s.22 threshold Rs20L (Rs10L special-category); s.2(6) aggregate turnover INCLUDES 'exports of goods or services'; Rule 96A, where LUT in RFD-11 is available only to a 'registered person'; s.24(i) and (iii) make inter-State suppliers and RCM payers compulsorily registered regardless of threshold. So the whole 'stay unregistered' advice rests on Notification 10/2017-IT exempting inter-State service suppliers, plus the NTOR rule.
